title: Two resistors in parallel
goal: See how the effective resistance of two resistors in parallel depends on the two resistances.
note: In a parallel circuit the current has two paths. The reciprocal of the effective resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the two resistances.

graphs.title: The effective resistance rises as the second resistance increases.
graphs.label: Effective resistance

graphs.title: Drag the point along the graph to change the resistance of the first resistor and watch the effective resistance.
graphs.label: Effective resistance

sentences: Two resistors are joined in parallel to the same supply.
The effective resistance of the combination is less than the smaller of the two resistances.

predict.prompt: Two resistors are joined in parallel. Will the effective resistance be larger or smaller than the smaller of the two resistances?
predict.reveal: Compare the effective resistance with the two resistances as you change them.

concept_check.question: What happens to the effective resistance when a second resistor is joined in parallel with a resistor?
concept_check.explanation: The current gains another path, so the effective resistance becomes smaller. The reciprocal of the effective resistance is the sum of the reciprocals, which is larger than either one.

hints: In a parallel circuit the current can take two paths.
Is the effective resistance larger or smaller than the smaller resistance?
Add the reciprocals of the two resistances, then take the reciprocal of the sum.
